title: Second lines, traffic and police over parades
summary: He discusses parade permits, traffic and streetcar routes, and monthly gatherings of old musicians.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Well, when is it going to be? Are they going to have one? No. Maybe they won't even have it, huh?

They ain't going to have it. They wouldn't give them no punishment. I wonder. Well, they overdo the thing. You understand what I mean? They block up all them buses. And that second line, they take us all over. You understand what I mean? They can have a parade like they're supposed to have it. No, they don't want to do right. They can have it and keep the traffic. Keep out that traffic streetway. Now, all jokes out. I'm playing white parade with Cornwall Freed. Them boys don't have no trouble. They don't have no traffic.

You got to give them. They don't have no traffic. Their parade goes on. It's smooth as anything. And they come down to no business street. On the street, be tied to be St. Charles. Well, they got it tied up on the counter for the wrecks. Yeah, yeah. Well, that's special. They got it special for that. Another thing. You see, we don't beat the wrecks at St. Charles and Louisiana Avenue. Yeah. You can't come down to St. Charles. No, that's right. You got the wrecks that beat most around Malcolm E. Coming up, we better be going nothing. See, the wrecks is right. Even when we had Louisiana Avenue, you don't go down Louisiana Avenue. They don't let you go. You have to take the magazine. Go down the magazine. That's right. That's what I like about it. And see, going down to St. Charles, we be going. We just like horses going down there. Playing all the way. Going all the time. The wrecks be coming up on one side, and we coming down. That's our life. It's our life in the story of the bunch of musicians. And it's kicking, talking to one another, and having fun. We talking about old things. And you see, all the old fellas you ain't seen, and once a month you take a day to be living. On the corner down St. Charles Street. Some of them old times you've been.
Yeah, you see a lot of fellas.
